newsitem.title: GERMANY: Union protest at German steel merger to go ahead.
newsitem.headline: Union protest at German steel merger to go ahead.

text.p: A protest by tens thousands of steel workers against merger plans for Thyssen AG and Fried. Krupp AG Krupp-Hoesch will go ahead despite news that Krupp has withdrawn plans for a hostile takeover, a workers' representative said on Monday.

Krupp last week launched an unsolicited bid to buy Thyssen, but agreed under political pressure to discuss merging the firms' steel operations instead, accounting for about one-third of combined turnover. On Monday the firms said Krupp was irrevocably withdrawing its buyout offer.
The steel workers plan to gather on Tuesday in Germany's financial capital Frankfurt to protest against the role of the banks in the merger bid, which Krupp alone does not have the money to finance.
"We have achieved a partial success, but we are going to demonstrate all the same," Georg Bongen, the head of Thyssen's workers' council, told Reuters.
